findings.evidence: lens D: Draft lines 67-74 and the MDX scorecard are identical (table.py: 'mdx table == draft table: True'). Both have 8 table lines with 5 pipes each, so the header, separator and 6 rows are well formed. Each row matches results.json: L1 has n_meeting 1 of n 5 ('One of five', does not hold); L2 has 2 of 6 (does not hold); L3 has 4 of 6 (holds); L4 has 1 of 6 (does not hold); household.L5.verdict has 2 of 6 (does not hold); household.L6.verdict has 1 of 6 (does not hold). The verdict words match each link's 'verdict' field. A difflib diff of draft/.rounds/5.json against 6.json shows that only the line '| Unemployment rises | Not tested (see the limits) | | |' left the table. git -C site diff shows the same single deletion in the MDX (line 126 of the live version). The template draft/if-msci-drops-indonesia.src.md:67-74 holds the same six bound rows with no unemployment row. The rows left are the six links the opening names (draft:5): stocks, rupiah, foreign money, prices, savings, borrowing.

findings.claim: After the owner had the unemployment bullet and the scorecard's 'Unemployment rises, not tested' row removed: does any sentence, heading, chart, alt text, excerpt or meta description in the post (draft and MDX) still refer to unemployment, jobs, the deleted bullet, or '(see the limits)' for it, or now read as if every feared link was tested when the fear chain as the post states it never included unemployment?
findings.evidence: lens D: terms.py ran a regex over the draft and the MDX for employ, job(s), labo(u)r, Sakernas, wage, work, crawler, Anthropic, 'AI tool', 'limits', 'not tested', 'could not', 'could check', every/each/all link, 'other links', BPS, L7 and 'the fears'. It found no mention of unemployment, jobs, Sakernas, the crawler or '(see the limits)'. The only 'limits' hit is the heading '## The limits of this test'. The 'not tested' hits are the food and fuel bullet; 'could not' is the 2005 policy rate (draft:59); the BPS hits are the CPI compiler and BPS's published inflation rates via Bank Indonesia, both still true. In the 5.json vs 6.json diff, the README, data/README, excerpt, metaDescription, seoTitle and all four alt texts are 'same', and none contains unemployment. I opened the four charts (mf-1 to mf-4). Their titles, labels and footnotes cover stocks, the rupiah, flows, inflation with fuel, and savings and loans; none mentions unemployment, and make_charts.py has no such term (its only 'limits' is 'axis limits' in a docstring). The opening states the chain as stocks, rupiah, foreign investors and the cost of living, then 'it reaches savings and the cost of borrowing' (draft:5). It never names unemployment, so 'I tested each link' and 'the other links do not' are now consistent with a six-row scorecard. They were less so in round 5, when a 'Not tested' row sat under 'I tested each link'. One soft residue: 'Twenty-two of the twenty-two predictions I could check came true' (draft:19). docs/2026-10-17-predictions-8.7.csv has 31 predictions and results.json household.predictions has n 22. Of the 9 unchecked, 7 are L7 (unemployment), 1 is L6 1997-09 and 1 is the 2005-08 policy note. The post now explains only the last of these (draft:59, 'for 2005, I could not find its rate for July'). The sentence is still true, and it does not refer to the deleted text.

findings.claim: gate.toml [claims] lost the entry 'I found no other official source with the same figures that I could use' (it licensed only the deleted bullet); amendment 8.10 was added to docs/2026-10-16-msci-fear-chain-design.md. Is 8.10 true in each statement (including that the README and data/README.md still record that the unemployment test was not run and why), and does any remaining [claims] or [allow] entry now refer to deleted text?
findings.evidence: lens D: Partly refuted. 8.10's last sentence says 'The README and `data/README.md` still record that the unemployment test was not run and why.' data/README.md:28 does record both: 'BPS's site blocks Anthropic's crawler in its robots file, so BPS's own pages and tables were not used, and the unemployment test could not be run: no other official source with BPS's round-by-round figures could be used.' README.md records only that the test was not run, with no reason: line 5 says 'Unemployment could not be tested. The samples are small, and the essay sets out the limits.' No other line of README.md (45 lines) gives a reason. After this change, the essay's limits no longer cover unemployment either. 'Still' is true: README.md and data/README.md match 5.json byte for byte, and git status shows neither changed. A second, smaller point: 8.10 puts quotation marks around 'Unemployment rises, not tested', but the deleted row was literally '| Unemployment rises | Not tested (see the limits) | | |'. The rest of 8.10 holds. The date 2026-10-19 New York time matches the files' mtime of Oct 19 18:58 EDT. 'After publication' holds: the MDX was in commit 64b141a on origin/main, with publishedAt 2026-10-18. '8.8, which reported L7 in the essay as not tested, with its reason' holds: 8.8 says 'L7 is reported as not tested, with this reason, in one sentence', and the deleted bullet was that sentence. 'No test rule or result changes' holds: git status lists only the design doc and gate.toml as modified; results.json, build_analysis.py and household.py are tracked and unchanged. On gate.toml, git diff shows exactly one line removed, the 'I found no other official source with the same figures that I could use' [claims] entry. entries.py found that none of the 33 [allow] phrases or 4 [claims] phrases appears in the 2 deleted lines, and none of the remaining reasons mentions unemployment or L7. Each remaining [claims] phrase still licenses live text. 'no other official source with BPS's round-by-round figures could be used' licenses data/README.md:28 (sources/provenance/rights-88 exists). The shock and slide definitions license the chart footnotes (make_charts.py:83-90). 'An episode counts for a link only once its outcome is known' licenses draft:23. | skeptic upheld: I re-checked this myself and the finding holds, at LOW severity. (1) README.md (45 lines) says only 'Unemployment could not be tested.' at line 5, and docs/README.src.md:5 is the same. Neither gives a reason. data/README.md:28 gives both the fact and the reason: BPS blocks the crawler, so 'the unemployment test could not be run: no other official source with BPS's round-by-round figures could be used.' Read plainly, 8.10 says both files record the reason, and README.md does not. A loose reading ('between them they record it') would make the sentence true, so this is an imprecise attribution, not a false result. (2) I diffed draft/.rounds/5.json against 6.json. The deleted row was exactly '| Unemployment rises | Not tested (see the limits) | | |' and the deleted bullet was the BPS/Anthropic crawler sentence. 8.10's quotation marks around 'Unemployment rises, not tested' therefore merge two cells, drop '(see the limits)' and change the capital. That is a paraphrase inside quotation marks, a minor fidelity point close to style. (3) The finding's other checks also hold: README.md and data/README.md match the 5.json texts byte for byte; git status lists only the design doc and gate.toml as modified; git diff of gate.toml removes exactly the one 'I found no other official source with the same figures...' [claims] line; the 'no other official source with BPS's round-by-round figures could be used' claim still licenses data/README.md:28; all four files have an mtime of 2026-10-19 18:58 EDT; the MDX has publishedAt 2026-10-18 and commit 64b141a is on origin/main; and no 'unemploy', 'jobs' or 'see the limits' remains in the draft .src.md, the .md or the MDX. One side effect is worth noting: README.md:5 still says 'Unemployment could not be tested... the essay sets out the limits', but the essay no longer mentions unemployment, so 8.10's suggestion that the README fully covers the reason is weaker still.
findings.fix: 8.10 narrowed: 'the scorecard row "Unemployment rises, not tested"' became 'the scorecard row on unemployment'; deleted 'and why' from the last sentence. Design doc only; the gate passes and scope --since 6 lists 0 changed sentences.

findings.claim: The deleted bullet was the essay's only statement that AI tools were used for the analysis
findings.evidence: lens D (note for the owner, not a defect): The deleted bullet was the post's only disclosure that AI tools are used for this analysis ('Anthropic makes the AI tools I use for this analysis'). It was also the post's only reason for taking BPS figures through Bank Indonesia and the IMF rather than from BPS. A grep of the draft, its .src.md template and the MDX for 'AI', 'Anthropic', 'Claude' and 'crawler' now returns nothing. The remaining BPS sentences (draft:41, 90, 92) are still true as written. data/README.md:28 keeps the crawler reason. This is the owner's editorial choice, not a factual error. It is flagged only so the owner knows the AI-use disclosure leaves the essay along with the bullet.
